title: [finding] `os migrate recorded-by --apply --json` prints a second JSON document `{"error":"EEXIT: 0"}` and exits 1 after a completed run (the command's catch re-reports oclif's exit signal)
body:
Source: the os-dev report on #21391 (`5956238556`, PR #21432), `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, class a. Filed by the `domain:cli` seat, `session_01VvcEokUG1tvVxkceYfR5XB`.

## What happens (measured, public door)

- **Setup:** a copy of the `examples/app-crm` repro database plus one `sys_metadata_history` row whose `recorded_by` is `system`, with the CLI built at `77a89b7b53`.
- **Command:** `os migrate recorded-by --apply --yes --json`.
- **Result:**
  - the row is converted (now `NULL`);
  - the command prints its result document;
  - then it prints a **second** document, `{"error":"EEXIT: 0"}`;
  - and it **exits 1**.
- A completed apply reports failure, and `--json` stdout carries two documents.

## Why (read from the code)

`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recorded-by.ts` emits its result, then calls `this.exit(result.status === 'completed' ? 0 : 1)` inside its `try`. Its `catch` has no `isExitSignal` rethrow, so oclif's `ExitError` for exit 0 is caught and re-reported as an error.

## The family (read, not all measured)

- `os migrate resume --run` has the same shape by reading. NOT MEASURED.
- `os migrate value-shapes` had it too. PR #21432 fixes that one, because its read-only scan now reaches the path.
- The fix is the existing idiom: rethrow on `isExitSignal` (from `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`), as the other `--json` commands do. A pin per command asserts one document and the exit code on a completed run.

Dedupe words: EEXIT second JSON document; recorded-by apply exits 1 after completed; catch re-reports oclif ExitError; migrate resume --run json exit.
